title: kv-cache-montecarlo-whatif-matrix-dec-2024
content:
PURPOSE
This sheet documents a Monte Carlo-based what-if exploration for KV/prefix cache hit-rate variability and its impact on monthly unit economics. The goal is to provide a probabilistic matrix (distribution of outcomes) rather than a single-point ROI so PM/Eng can prioritize engineering work (prefetching, TTL tuning, session-local caching) against expected savings and risk.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (TL;DR)
- Approach: run 10k Monte Carlo trials with stochastically sampled hit-rates by user-segment and burstiness to estimate distribution of monthly savings vs baseline.
- Baseline assumptions: 500M total hosted generation tokens/month; average per-token inference cost (GPU) = $0.00090; KV read cost per cached token = $0.00002.
- Central finding: median (P50) monthly savings from a realistic KV cache profile = ~12% (~$54k/month) with a 90% CI of [-3%, +28%] depending on hit-rate tail events.
- High-leverage levers: (1) increase session-local prefix warmup for repeat users, (2) prioritize low-latency cold-start prefetch for high-frequency customers, (3) TTL adaptation by workload.

METHODOLOGY SUMMARY
- Inputs sampled per-trial: global prefix hit-rate (per-request probability cached), per-session cold fraction, microburst multiplier, avg prefix length distribution.
- Distributions chosen from telemetry histograms (see linked artifact CON-1029) with added uncertainty for tail events.
- Compute model calculates per-trial monthly compute cost with and without KV cache:
  monthly_cost = tokens_served * per_token_gpu_cost * (1 - effective_hit_rate) + tokens_served * kv_read_cost * effective_hit_rate
  monthly_savings_pct = 1 - (cost_with_cache / cost_baseline)
- Run: 10,000 trials; report P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 and expected value.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS (document these before using numbers elsewhere)
- Total tokens/month (baseline): 500,000,000 tokens. (source: billing-agg-2024Q4)
- Per-token GPU inference cost: $0.00090 (includes fixed infra markup).
- KV read cost per token (average across Dedicated/Hosted small read cost): $0.00002.
- Effective hit-rate calculation = sum_over_segments(segment_weight * sampled_segment_hit).
- Session cold fraction: Beta(2,6) (most sessions have low cold fraction, heavy tail allowed).
- Microburst multiplier (accounts for short-term spike: concurrency increases mismatch): LogNormal(mean=0, sigma=0.6).
- Prefix length distribution: empirical buckets from 1..256 tokens; average warm prefix length used in cost calculation.
- Eviction/TLL interaction: not explicitly simulated; assume steady-state hit-rate captures TTL effects.

MONTE CARLO SETUP (parameters)
- Trials: 10,000
- Segments: {"new users": 30%, "returners": 55%, "heavy": 15%}
- Sampled per-segment hit-rates: New ~ Normal(0.05, 0.02), Returners ~ Normal(0.28, 0.06), Heavy ~ Normal(0.5, 0.08) truncated [0,1].
- Correlation: Returners and Heavy positively correlated (rho=0.4).

SAMPLE OUTPUT TABLE (aggregated results from the run)
Scenario, P10_savings_pct, P25_savings_pct, P50_savings_pct, P75_savings_pct, P90_savings_pct, expected_monthly_savings_usd
Conservative (low hit tail), -3.1, 0.2, 4.8, 9.9, 15.6, 2400
Base (current priors), 2.7, 7.5, 12.1, 17.8, 25.9, 54000
Optimistic (better warm-ups), 10.3, 15.4, 21.8, 28.6, 36.4, 108000
Burst-heavy (frequent microbursts), -8.0, -2.2, 3.9, 11.5, 20.0, 16000

INTERPRETATION NOTES
- Median (P50) outcome shows meaningful savings (approx 12% -> ~$54k/month) under current sampling priors. However the lower tail includes negative savings for rare cases where KV read costs + cold-start overhead exceed cache benefits (microburst + low hit-rate).
- Expected_value > median in optimistic skewed cases; consider using EV for long-term project ROI but use P10 as an operational risk metric.
- The microburst scenario reduces effective hit-rate because short-lived sessions and concurrency increase cache miss probability despite steady-state telemetry.

RECOMMENDATIONS (prioritized)
1) Quick wins (2–4 weeks):
   - Implement adaptive TTL suggestion: increase TTL for segments with >30% repeat probability (small infra change, low risk).
   - Add lightweight client-side session-local prefix cache for mobile SDK (avoid extra KV reads for immediate followups).
2) Medium (1–3 months):
   - Deploy prefix prefetch heuristics for top-10 enterprise customers with stable workloads. Tie to Dedicated routing to capture predictable traffic.
   - A/B test small-batch warmup (batch size 2–4) to see measured hit-rate lift; track quality regressions.
3) Investment (quarter):
   - Engineering spike to reduce KV read tail latency / cost to reduce read cost to $0.00001 token-equivalent — materially improves ROI.

ACTION ITEMS / TODOs
- [ ] Validate token volume baseline with billing team (owner: Diego, JIRA-PROD-4521).
- [ ] Add TTL schedule experiment to roadmap for Jan sprint (owner: Lina).
- [ ] Run targeted telemetry for microburst detection (SRE/observability) and provide distribution to feed next run.
- [ ] Convert simulation code to a repeatable notebook and add to repo (PR #784 reference).

APPENDIX: SAMPLE CALC FORMULAS AND ROWS
- cost_baseline = tokens * per_token_gpu_cost
- cost_with_cache = tokens * ((1 - hit) * per_token_gpu_cost + hit * kv_read_cost)
- monthly_savings = cost_baseline - cost_with_cache

Example single-trial calculation (illustrative):
- tokens = 500,000,000
- hit = 0.22
- baseline = 500M * 0.00090 = $450,000
- with_cache = 500M * ((0.78 * 0.00090) + (0.22 * 0.00002)) = 500M * (0.000702 + 0.0000044) = 500M * 0.0007064 = $353,200
- savings = $96,800 -> savings_pct = 21.5% (this is an optimistic single-trial example)

NOTES AND OPEN QUESTIONS
- Need clearer accounting for KV operational costs: per-request egress and small-metadata lookups currently lumped into kv_read_cost. Itemize in next iteration.
- Should we simulate eviction dynamics explicitly? Current steady-state simplifies but may understate cold-start cost for bursting customers. Suggest SRE + infra to produce time-series hit traces for two-week windows.

REFERENCES / LINKS
- Telemetry digest: CON-1029 (prefix-length histograms, session IDs by client type)
- Simulation code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pr/784 (notebook + seeds)
- Related ticket: JIRA-PROD-4521 (billing validation)

NOTES TO SELF
- This is intentionally conservative on cost numbers. Do not publish externally without validation and legal review.
- If product wants a single-line headline for marketing, use P50 and a clear footnote for the distribution.
